articles.title: No pressure, no problem: Superconductor record shattered after 30 years
articles.summary: A team at the University of Houston has achieved superconductivity at 151 Kelvin under ambient pressure—the highest ever. That's 18 degrees warmer than the previous record set in 1993. The breakthrough uses a pressure-quenching technique, making the material stable at normal conditions and bringing room-temperature superconductors one step closer.

articles.title: Rock clouds that vanish: JWST reveals extreme weather on distant exoplanet
articles.summary: Using the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers have observed a daily cloud cycle on the Hot Jupiter WASP-94A b. Morning skies are filled with magnesium silicate clouds, but by evening they disappear—possibly evaporating in 1,000°C heat. The finding, published in Science, offers an unprecedented clear view of an exoplanet's atmosphere.

articles.title: Hidden engines of monster supernovae revealed by NASA's Fermi telescope
articles.summary: After nearly 20 years of searching, NASA's Fermi telescope has detected definitive gamma rays from a superluminous supernova, SN 2017egm. The data, published in Astronomy & Astrophysics, strongly supports the theory that these ultra-bright explosions are powered by magnetars—rapidly spinning neutron stars with magnetic fields 10 trillion times stronger than a refrigerator magnet.
